$comment: Wire contract for POST /api/geek-crawler/internal/rag/index-status. HAND-MAINTAINED, not generated: an earlier version of this comment claimed it was generated from IndexStatusResponse, and no generator has ever existed. One could not be complete anyway -- eventType is added by webhook.notify() after model_dump, and the C# type strings and these notes are not derivable from a Pydantic model. GeekBackend keeps a copy whose `fields` map must match this one; a test on each side pins its own half, and the cross-repo workflow compares the two maps. Neither repo can see the other's types at compile time, so this file is the only thing standing between them. It exists because on 2026-09-29 five fields were found to be sent on every webhook and bound by nothing: pagesSkippedUnusable, attempt, trigger, embeddingRateLimitRetries, embeddingWaitSeconds. Dropping pagesSkippedUnusable meant a run whose corpus was gutted by 4xx error pages was indistinguishable from one that indexed cleanly, because the two benign skip reasons were bound and the one that indicts the crawl was not.
auth: X-API-Key, whose value must equal GeekAPI's GEEK_BACKEND_API_KEY. The sender reads INDEX_STATUS_WEBHOOK_KEY and falls back to its own API_KEY when that is unset (app.py), and API_KEY is a different secret -- so the header name is always right and the value is wrong by default. ApiKeyMiddleware compares ordinally and 401s on mismatch. The sender logs that at ERROR rather than WARNING precisely because it means every webhook is rejected, not one.

$notes.eventType: Not on the model. webhook.notify() adds it to the payload after model_dump, so it is on the wire and must be in this list.
$notes.persisted: GeekAPI persists five of these to crawl_runs as Rag* fields: state, chunksUpserted, pagesEnglish, pagesSkippedUnusable, finishedAtUtc. The rest reach SignalR and the crawls/{runId}/rag-index projection only. The receiver refuses an absent run 404 before any write, and a persist that matches no document or raises answers 404 or 502 rather than Accepted (GeekBackend 2123a1b, deployed 2026-09-30). A 202 therefore means the five fields were written. The sender logs 404 and 5xx at ERROR naming that crawl_runs still carries stale numbers (Geek-Crawler-Rag 406a77c).
$notes.attempt: Bound and pushed but deliberately NOT used by the receiver's out-of-order guard, which keys on finishedAtUtc. Changing that is a behaviour decision, not a binding one.
$notes.comparison: Only the `fields` map is compared across repos. Prose in $comment and $notes may differ, so editing a note here does not red the other repo's main.
